conclusion: Not a misstatement: control passes at a point in time, only upon physical delivery and signed customer acceptance (CON-C02-T1). Payment is due 30 days after acceptance (CON-C02-T2); the supplied terms do not address return rights, rebates, bill-and-hold, consignment, guarantees or related-party arrangements.

CON-C02-T2 states: “Payment is due 30 days after acceptance.”
Revenue is recognised when or as the customer obtains control of the promised good or service.

Revenue is recognised over time only if at least one of the criteria in paragraph 35 is met; otherwise, the performance obligation is satisfied at a point in time, considering indicators of control transfer including physical possession and customer acceptance.

The supplied contract terms do not address return rights, rebates, bill-and-hold, consignment, guarantees or related-party arrangements, so their presence or absence cannot be confirmed beyond the terms provided.

The stated control-transfer event is physical delivery together with signed customer acceptance under CON-C02-T1, indicating a point-in-time transfer rather than a transfer over time. CON-C02-T2 sets the payment timing after acceptance; no other relevant terms are identified in the supplied terms.

counter_argument: A conflicting executed contract term or amendment stating that control passes before physical delivery and signed customer acceptance would overturn the identified transfer point.
